title: Spec Tasks list omits shipped procs flush_maybe_duck and bed_duck_ratio, despite its change log claiming the drift was fixed
evidence:
+    procs `bed_update` (stream update + envelope + `SetMusicVolume`),
+    `bed_envelope_step` (pure envelope transitions), `bed_duck_trigger`
+    (called from `audio_flush` via the `pending_any_plays` helper),
+    `bed_duck_multiplier` (pure, capped at 1.0 — the duck never raises the
+    bed), `bed_level` (pure: master × pause × duck), `pending_any_plays`;
... vs ...
+  guards/sha256). Known-bad state avoided: a reviewer diffing spec against
+  code finds procs that don't exist.
... vs code ...
+flush_maybe_duck :: proc(a: ^Audio) {
+bed_duck_ratio :: proc(master, duck: f32) -> f32 {
detail: The change log says Tasks were amended to 'the real names' so spec/code diffing finds no missing procs, yet the r1-fold procs flush_maybe_duck and bed_duck_ratio ship in code and appear nowhere in Tasks; the trigger call-chain description is also wrong.
recommended_fix: Add flush_maybe_duck and bed_duck_ratio to the spec Tasks list and correct the chain to audio_flush → flush_maybe_duck (pending_any_plays) → bed_duck_trigger.

title: 'before-the-clear ordering ... unit-pinned' is false: no added test drives audio_flush
evidence:
+// (check BEFORE the pending clear) live in flush_maybe_duck — unit-
+// pinned (Perkins r1 W1).
... and ...
+// the trigger wiring is unit-pinned here — the predicate, the trigger, and
+// the before-the-clear ordering in ONE testable proc).
... corroborated in-diff (verif-gap.txt) ...
+   Audio{bed_on = true} — none calls audio_flush or bed_update. Symbol searches: audio_flush appears only
detail: The ordering is the call-site placement of flush_maybe_duck before 'a.pending = {}' inside audio_flush; tests call flush_maybe_duck directly with hand-set pending, so moving the call after the clear fails no test. The unit-pinned claim overstates coverage.
recommended_fix: Reword comments to claim only predicate/trigger pinning, or restructure so a pure test can observe audio_flush's trigger-before-clear ordering headlessly.

title: pending_any_plays re-encodes the play-family list; a future fifth family silently misses the duck
detail: The r1-flagged OR-list duplication survives the fold: adding a Pending family requires updating this predicate in lockstep with the flush's play loops, and test_flush_duck_wiring enumerates only the four known families, so an omission fails no test.
recommended_fix: Share one family registry between the flush play loops and the duck predicate, or add a reflective test over all Pending fields so a forgotten family fails loudly.

title: bed_on gate applied to step/trigger but not to bed_duck_multiplier/bed_level
detail: The r1 note-12 fold gates bed_envelope_step on bed_on ('a bed_off Audio has no envelope, ever') yet leaves the multiplier/level readers ungated; any stale envelope state on a bed_off Audio would still duck the computed level.
recommended_fix: Gate bed_duck_multiplier/bed_level on bed_on for symmetry, or document explicitly why only the mutating procs require the gate.

title: Build script guards every input except a missing ffmpeg, which still dies with a raw traceback
evidence:
+# --- guards (r1 review: actionable failures, no silent garbage) -----------
...
+ffmpeg_ver = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30).stdout.splitlines()[0]
detail: The guard section added SystemExit failures for missing/mismatched vault input, sampwidth, channels, and window fit, but a missing ffmpeg still raises FileNotFoundError at the -version probe — the exact failure class the section claims to eliminate.
recommended_fix: Probe with shutil.which('ffmpeg') or wrap the -version call in try/except and SystemExit with an actionable install message before any subprocess use.

title: 24MB WAV intermediate is never deleted by the script — cleanup is only a docstring instruction
evidence:
+Output: assets/audio/ambience_loop.ogg (committed, ~0.9MB, vorbis 48kHz
+stereo, 125.6s) + a same-named .wav intermediate (24MB — delete it; it is
+the encode source, not a repo artifact).
detail: Nothing in the 149-line script removes OUT_WAV after a successful encode; every run leaves a 24MB artifact on disk indefinitely, with the new .gitignore rule as the only mitigation against accidental commit.
recommended_fix: os.remove(OUT_WAV) after the encode succeeds (or emit the intermediate to a temp directory), keeping the .gitignore entry as belt-and-braces.

title: PR body scratch file committed at the repo root
evidence:
diff --git a/_pr_body_ambience.md b/_pr_body_ambience.md
new file mode 100644
detail: A PR-body draft lands as a tracked top-level file; its content belongs in the PR description, not the tree, and it begins rotting the moment the PR merges.
recommended_fix: Drop _pr_body_ambience.md from the commit (or relocate under the _bmad-output convention) and paste the content into the actual PR body.

detail: The three transcripts carry prompt echoes, shell dumps, and status-bar chrome, and they document a pre-fold diff whose findings (e.g. uncapped duck ratio) contradict the shipped code — verif-gap.txt itself admits the staleness in-file.
